source_text: Nonne illi coniuges primi, quorum nuptias benedixit Deus, dicens: Crescite et multiplicamini , nudi erant, et non confundebantur ? Cur ergo ex illis membris confusio post peccatum, nisi quia exstitit illic indecens motus, quem, nisi homines peccassent, procul dubio nuptiae non haberent?
pass_a_gloss: Not? illi coniuges primi, quorum marriages benedixit God, dicens: Crescite and multiplicamini, nudi erant, and not confundebantur? why therefore from those members confusio after sin, unless because exstitit there indecens movement, whom, unless human-beings peccassent, far dubio marriages not haberent?

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: “Were not the first spouses, whose marriage God blessed by saying, ‘Increase and multiply’ (Genesis 1:28), naked and unashamed (Genesis 2:25)? Why, then, did shame about those organs follow sin, unless an indecent movement arose there, which marriage would certainly not have had if human beings had not sinned?”

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.
